description: Optional revised comprehensive and hardware finals. Legacy exams and scores remain unchanged.

exams.title: Systems and Networking Comprehensive Final — Revised V4
questions: A workstation has address 192.168.18.21/24. Which network is correct?
192.168.18.21 with a 24-bit network prefix is in 192.168.18.0/24. The .21 is its host portion; /32 describes only that host, not its subnet.
Which address is the broadcast of a typical 10.2.3.0/24 network?
For 10.2.3.0/24, all eight host bits set to one yield broadcast 10.2.3.255. The .1 host address and 10.2.4.255 lie elsewhere.
An IP address works but a domain fails. What do you inspect?
Verify IP gateway forwarding before checking the configured DNS resolver
Inspect file permissions on the client rather than query the hostname
DNS resolution
An IP address working while a name fails narrows investigation toward DNS resolver settings, records or lookup behavior. It does not prove that every route or service works.
A web server returns HTTP 404. What is confirmed?
No DNS lookup ever worked
An HTTP response was received
The server was breached
A received HTTP 404 confirms an HTTP server produced a response, ordinarily that the requested resource was unavailable. It does not establish a breach or explain all preceding DNS traffic.
Which resource is volatile working memory?
RAM
SSD
Backup tape
RAM is ordinarily volatile working memory. SSDs and magnetic or other backup media retain content without power, subject to their own reliability limitations.
A Linux file has mode 640. What can the owning group do?
Modify the file
Execute the file
Read the file
In ordinary Unix mode 640, the middle digit 4 gives group read without write or execute. ACLs and contextual enforcement can further affect effective access.
A high-CPU process begins during an approved nightly backup. What follows?
Assume the schedule proves the process is safe and need not be checked
Compare schedule and logs before concluding
Stop the backup job immediately before gathering relevant logs
High CPU aligned with scheduled backups is a correlation, not conclusive evidence of safety or intrusion. Review the job, service identity and relevant logs before intervention.
What should happen after a patch?
Verify installed version and key workflows
Close the ticket without checks
Remove all logs
Patch installation alone does not confirm closure. Verify installed version, the originally broken condition, essential user workflows and any regressions using approved tests.
Which information helps make a help-desk ticket reproducible?
The latest ticket status without a user-impact description
A generic device model without a symptom or time reference
Timestamp, symptoms and tests performed
A reproducible ticket needs observed symptoms, timestamps, scope and exact diagnostic steps. Ambiguous labels and unnecessary private data undermine safe troubleshooting.
Which is a safe first step in an unfamiliar terminal?
Run commands as root without review
Read command documentation and expected effects
Erase unknown directories
Unknown commands should be reviewed for effects, privilege requirements and scope before execution. A terminal is not inherently safe just because it is used for learning.
What helps restore a lost file reliably?
Tested versioned backup
A sync-only mirror with no history
Changing the filename
A versioned backup tested by restoring representative data provides better recovery evidence than a live mirror without history or a renamed file.
What is a gateway's common purpose?
Decrypt every website
Grant file permissions
Forward traffic toward another network
A gateway commonly forwards traffic between networks using routing information. It does not independently grant file permissions or decrypt all application content.

exams.title: Defensive Security and Incident Response Comprehensive Final — Revised V4
courses: Applied Security Architecture and Threat Modeling
questions: A sign-in log contains two failures. What is proven?
Two failed password entries establish a successful intrusion
Two failures were recorded
Every account on the server is now compromised
Two failed sign-ins establish two recorded failures under the logging conditions. They do not prove a successful attacker login or compromise of unrelated accounts.
A failed login and later successful login are observed. What should you do?
Correlate identity, source and authorized activity
Assume credential theft
Publish password records
A failure followed by success may reflect a legitimate typo or abuse. Correlate subject, source, device, time and approved behavior before attributing cause.
Which statement best defines least privilege?
Grant every worker administrator access
Never review permissions
Grant only access required for the task
Least privilege limits each identity to actions and resources justified by its task. Overly broad administrator grants increase impact and make access reviews difficult.
A private signing key appears in public source. What's required?
Change the code formatting
Revoke or rotate and investigate
Ignore the previous commit
Public exposure of a signing private key threatens the assurance of signatures made with it. Revoke or rotate as applicable and review past signing activity and trust.
What does an authenticated cryptographic digest comparison help check?
File integrity
Guaranteed absence of software flaws
Employee job title
Comparing a file digest with an authenticated expected value can detect changed bytes. It does not guarantee the absence of vulnerabilities or identify a person's job.
What does full-disk encryption chiefly protect?
Network uptime
Physical screen protection
Confidentiality of stored data
Full-disk encryption chiefly protects data at rest when devices are lost or offline. It does not guarantee network availability or prevent every misuse after sign-in.
An urgent supplier bank-change email is received. What should finance do?
Call the number in the message
Verify using a previously trusted channel
Approve based on its logo
Payment detail changes must be verified using contact information established before the suspicious message. Calling numbers supplied in the message repeats the same trust boundary.
A risk rating should account for which factors?
Exposure, impact and uncertainty
The scanner's highest score without considering attack exposure
The most recent warning regardless of asset importance
Exposure, business impact, likelihood and unknowns inform operational risk. Device price or an interface color does not establish technical severity.
An incident report should distinguish what?
Officer rank and wallpaper
Private passwords and tokens
Confirmed facts and working hypotheses
Incident reports separate confirmed observations from hypotheses, evidence limits and untested claims. Without that distinction, readers may mistake correlation for attribution.
What is a useful detection metric?
Total number of alerts regardless of usefulness
Share of alerts requiring meaningful action
Number of dashboards configured without outcome measurement
The share of useful alerts helps assess signal quality. Large dashboard counts can reflect duplication or noisy rules without improving detection.
A backup job succeeds every day but no restore was tested. What's missing?
Controlled restoration evidence
More optimistic status messages
Administrative credentials in a public file
Backup job completion measures a process outcome, not application recoverability. An isolated restore must validate data, dependencies and elapsed recovery time.
A team's production change precedes a service outage. What is justified?
Proof of deliberate attack
Proof the change is unrelated
A temporal correlation deserving investigation
A change preceding an outage deserves investigation but temporal proximity alone does not prove intent or causality. Reconstruct the timeline and compare alternate causes.

exams.title: Authorized Assessment and Web Cloud Comprehensive Final — Revised V4
questions: A target isn't in written scope. What should the assessor do?
Test after office hours
Request additional permission before testing
Assume a related brand is permission
Written authorization defines targets and techniques. A related brand or after-hours timing does not make an excluded endpoint permissible to test.
A student's browser hides another user's grade link. What enforces privacy?
Backend record authorization
A browser-side role flag that hides unauthorized buttons
A UI route guard without a backend object check
Hiding a link in a browser cannot enforce private-record access. A trusted backend must check identity and object-level authorization on each request.
Which design mitigates SQL query manipulation?
String concatenation of untrusted input
Disabled error handling
Parameterized queries
Parameterized SQL queries keep untrusted values separate from SQL syntax. Raw concatenation is unsafe; hiding error output is not an injection prevention mechanism.
A student signs out. What must session design consider?
Replacing the profile photo after pressing logout
Expiry and invalidation of authentication state
Clearing the login text box without invalidating tokens
Sign-out design must invalidate or expire applicable session tokens, especially for privileged access. Cosmetic profile changes do not revoke active authorization.
A cloud storage bucket contains public images and private grades. Best design?
Separate access policies by data classification
Make all objects public
Disable auditing
Public assets and private student grades need different resource grants. Enforce classification in server rules or object policies, with negative access tests.
An app includes a privileged cloud token in client JavaScript. What is the risk?
The token is secret if the filename is obscure
CSS prevents access
Public client delivery exposes privileged credentials
A privileged token in delivered browser code is exposed to anyone who can inspect public assets. Obscure filenames or CSS cannot protect it.
A service account needs one report bucket. What is best?
Global administrator privileges
Scoped permission for the required bucket
Shared employee passwords
A service identity needing one report bucket should have only the relevant actions on that bucket. Shared passwords or global admin grants expand privilege unnecessarily.
What does a four-hour RPO measure?
Tolerated loss of recent data
Guaranteed recovery in four hours
Encryption strength
A four-hour RPO means up to four hours of recent changes may be lost at recovery, not that service is restored in four hours. Recovery time is RTO.
Which finding is reproducible?
A high severity label with no reproduction method
A vendor summary without observed conditions on the tested asset
Scope, observed condition, evidence, effect and retest
Reproducible findings include authorized scope, exact observations, impact, relevant controls and measurable retest. Dramatic labels do not substitute for evidence.
When is a remediation finding ready for closure?
Immediately after a fix is proposed
After approved retest and documented outcome
After deleting the logs
Close a finding only after approved retests demonstrate the original weakness is corrected and required functions still operate. Proposed patches are not evidence of deployment.
A public demo application returns an unexpected synthetic record. What may be claimed?
Behavior observed only in the authorized demo
Production data was stolen
Every endpoint is vulnerable
Unexpected synthetic data may indicate a flaw in the controlled demo; it does not establish exploitation or data exposure in production.
What makes an executive security summary useful?
Only raw system events
Guaranteed elimination of cyber risk
Risks, evidence, options, limitations and owners
Executives need evidenced risk, decision options, tradeoffs, owners and limitations. Raw logs alone or impossible guarantees are not a decision-ready summary.

exams.title: Evidence Interpretation and Decision-Making Final — Revised V4
questions: Synthetic log: 09:00 failed, 09:01 failed, 09:04 success. Which conclusion is justified?
Successful compromise has been proven
Three authentication outcomes were recorded; account intent remains unknown
No further context is useful
The synthetic sequence shows two failures then one success. Without source, actor and authorization context, the records alone do not establish compromise intent.
The user reports a lost security key. Which first response respects procedure?
Disable all organizational security logging
Ask for their password in chat
Verify identity via an approved recovery process
Lost security-key recovery should follow a verified identity and account-recovery process. Requesting passwords or disabling logs introduces additional risk.
A monitoring dashboard's alerts doubled after a rule change. What should be compared?
Rule changes, actual events and false-positive rates
Only the updated rule's name and dashboard appearance
The raw count alone without examining false-positive rates
More alerts after a rule update can reflect increased coverage or noise. Compare change configuration, underlying events, precision and analyst workload.
A suspected incident and a known software update share a timestamp. What should the analyst write?
The update certainly caused a breach
Temporal association; cause not yet established
The alert is certainly harmless
Two events sharing a timestamp may be related or coincidental. Correlation should be documented while alternative causes and evidence gaps remain open.
Which report statement is evidence bounded?
All company records have leaked
No vulnerabilities can exist
Supplied records show denied requests from a synthetic test account
A denied synthetic request supports only that observed denial in the supplied setting. It cannot prove every record secure or every production system breached.
A firewall change makes a payroll app unavailable. Which evidence matters before rollback?
Approved change record, observed effect and rollback criteria
Only the affected device's router hostname
A guessed policy change unsupported by the actual change record
An access-control change disrupting payroll requires reference to the approved change, actual impact, rollback criteria and affected service owners before action.
Which classification fits an event recorded but not corroborated?
Confirmed attacker attribution
Observation with unresolved interpretation
Proven customer data loss
An uncorroborated record is an observation whose meaning is uncertain. Attribution and claims of customer loss require independent supporting evidence.
A mock host shows inode use 100% but blocks 40%. What is the best diagnosis?
Data-block exhaustion despite only 40% block consumption
A DNS lookup failure that necessarily prevents file creation
Metadata entry exhaustion may block new files
With inodes at 100% but storage blocks only 40% used, the file system can fail to create new directory entries despite free bytes. Inspect inode allocation safely.
A user receives a payment change request from a lookalike domain. What is the appropriate action?
Independently verify with a previously known supplier contact
Send credentials to the sender
Approve because the subject says urgent
Lookalike domains and urgent supplier payment requests warrant independent verification via a previously trusted number. Replying in the same message channel is insufficient.
A log collection has a gap. What follows?
The missing interval can be treated as confirmed no activity
The gap limits confidence in conclusions
A gap necessarily proves deliberate log tampering
Missing log periods limit conclusions about events in the gap. The absence of records neither establishes a clean interval nor proves an attacker removed logs.
A report contains a screenshot with a session token. What should be done?
Publish the token for transparency
Email the token widely
Redact and restrict evidence; consider token handling procedures
Session tokens in evidence should be redacted, access restricted and exposure assessed for revocation. Broad publication can turn a diagnostic artifact into a credential leak.
What is a meaningful recovery acceptance test?
Re-run the original business transaction and validate controls
Only confirm a reboot occurred
Close every investigation immediately
Recovery requires demonstrating original business transactions and relevant security controls after restoration. A reboot status is not evidence that business operations function.

exams.title: Cloud Identity and Software Assurance Final — Revised V4
courses: Beginner Python Logic and Defensive Automation
questions: A student can read another student's private grade through an API. Where is the primary fix?
Hide the profile icon
Trusted backend per-record authorization
Rename the grade field
A trusted API must check per-record authorization for every grade request. Hiding navigation elements cannot prevent someone from constructing direct API requests.
A read-only reporting service has global administrator rights. What is the risk?
Read-only work always requires admin
Access scope has no effect
Its permissions exceed the required task
Global administrator rights exceed the need for read-only reporting; narrow permissions to the exact data and operations, then validate positive and denied access.
A former contractor still has an active session. What should be verified?
Account disablement and actual session revocation across systems
Disabling the contractor's normal password but leaving sessions usable
Verifying only badge return without testing digital access
Contractor offboarding involves effective account disablement and revoking persistent sessions and delegated tokens across relevant services. A physical badge update alone is insufficient.
A cloud bucket policy allows all users to read every path. What is the proper review?
Keep wildcard grants for simplicity
Restrict grants to required public objects and verify denied private reads
Use unpredictable filenames instead of access checks
Wildcard cloud reads expose private resources regardless of obscure filenames. Limit policies to intended public objects, then verify private reads fail.
A build's digest mismatches an authenticated expected digest. What is supported?
The file is confirmed malware
All other dependencies are safe
The obtained content differs from the authenticated reference
A mismatch against an authenticated expected digest proves the fetched bytes differ from that trusted reference. It does not identify malware or certify every dependency.
A service token was accidentally placed in client-side code. What should happen?
Revoke or rotate exposed credential and move privilege to trusted service
Only minify the JavaScript
Assume nobody can read web assets
Exposed client-side tokens should be revoked or rotated and privileged operations moved server-side. Minifying JavaScript does not undo credential disclosure.
A recovery plan states RPO 4 hours. What does this describe?
The maximum time before service restoration must finish
Maximum tolerable recent data loss
The required frequency for rotating account passwords
RPO is tolerable recent data loss, measured by time from the incident to the latest acceptable recoverable point. Router reboot time concerns different availability objectives.
A cloud log omits an application trace ID. What improvement helps investigations?
A user email address stored alongside every secret token
A human-readable dashboard title instead of stable correlation IDs
Correlatable request identifiers with minimal sensitive content
Correlatable identifiers and minimized sensitive fields help trace cloud events across services. Logging all passwords undermines security and privacy.
A scripted event count receives an unknown status. What's safest?
Record invalid input separately
Silently treat as success
Invent a new confirmed attack
Unexpected event values should be recorded as invalid or unknown for review. Treating them as successes or inventing attacks corrupts monitoring results.
A Python counter receives failed, success, failed, unknown. How many valid failed events?
Three
Two
Four
Two entries in the supplied sequence are labeled failed. Unknown status is not a valid failure unless the documented classification rules say so.
An access control change works for administrators. What additional test matters?
Whether the login page has a logo
Whether all users can get admin
Approved standard user access and denied unauthorized access
After access-control changes, verify intended privileged and standard roles still work and unauthorized roles are denied. A logo or broad admin access is not evidence.
A production configuration differs from approved code. What should be done?
Investigate and document drift before applying a reviewed correction
Overwrite without backup or approval
Ignore if the app loads
Configuration drift should be compared with approved baseline and change records before scoped remediation. Blind overwrite can disrupt systems or destroy rollback evidence.

exams.title: PC Build, Repair and Diagnostic Decisions Examination — Revised V4
questions: An assembled desktop powers on but reports a DRAM error LED. What is the safest initial sequence?
Re-seat powered memory while the computer is running
Disconnect power, verify DIMM seating and compatibility, then retest POST
Replace the power supply before checking memory compatibility
A DRAM light after assembly narrows attention to memory initialization, not necessarily a failed module. Disconnect power, verify seating/compatibility and retest POST.
A motherboard requires both ATX 24-pin and EPS CPU power. Which connection is essential?
The dedicated CPU EPS connector in addition to motherboard power
Only the graphics card PCIe lead
A SATA data cable
Motherboards commonly need separate 24-pin ATX and EPS CPU power leads. Similar-looking PCIe connectors must not be substituted for the CPU EPS cable.
A computer shuts off under high CPU load after a cooler change. Which evidence is most useful?
The number of desktop icons while the system is idle
Only the power LED without any thermal measurement
CPU temperatures, cooler mounting, fan operation and thermal logs
Thermal shutdown after a cooler change calls for temperature trend, cooler installation, fan/pump behavior and logs. An unrelated desktop screenshot provides no evidence.
A new NVMe drive is not detected. What should be checked before declaring it defective?
The operating-system wallpaper and monitor refresh rate
M.2 slot protocol, firmware detection and lane-sharing restrictions
The file browser display language and default keyboard layout
NVMe recognition depends on slot protocol, firmware settings and possible shared lanes. Diagnose detection before declaring a drive defective or formatting anything.
What is the strongest evidence that a RAM-related repair succeeded?
POST passes, correct capacity is detected and repeatable memory checks succeed
A boot screen without memory capacity verification
A lit motherboard indicator without a repeatable test
Successful memory repair is evidenced by repeatable POST, expected capacity and controlled tests. Indicator lights and photographs cannot demonstrate sustained correctness.
Which action should be avoided during beginner PC servicing?
Documenting cable placement
Checking the motherboard manual
Opening a sealed power supply enclosure
Sealed power supplies can retain hazardous electrical charge even after unplugging. Never open one as a beginner; external documentation and safe cable checks are appropriate.
Two RAM modules on a dual-channel board should be installed according to:
The two closest-looking sockets regardless of the manual
The motherboard manual's recommended slot pairing
Whichever slots leave the most physical distance from the CPU
Dual-channel slot placement depends on motherboard wiring and manual guidance; visually adjacent slots may not be the recommended pair.
An upgrade seems slower after the system is repaired. What is the most defensible next step?
Compare baseline and current measurements under the same workload
Assume the SSD is counterfeit
Disable operating-system updates permanently
Use comparable baseline and current measurements with the same workload to assess upgrade performance. Unsupported counterfeiting claims or disabling updates are inappropriate.
A repair for a friend's PC is authorized. What must be addressed before inspecting private files?
Nothing; ownership grants unlimited access
An automatic cloud backup to your account
Permission scope, privacy boundaries, backup responsibility and reversible changes
Owner approval must cover privacy boundaries, data handling, backup responsibility and reversible changes. Permission to repair is not permission to inspect private accounts.

exams.title: Workstation, Virtualization and Home Lab Readiness Examination — Revised V4
courses: Red Team Workstation & Home Lab Engineering
questions: A deliberately vulnerable practice VM is on the same bridged network as household devices. What should be done first?
Keep the bridged network but avoid opening a browser
Disconnect the guest and move it to an isolated virtual segment before testing
Permit access by relying only on the guest's private IP
Intentionally vulnerable guests should not be bridged onto household segments. Disconnect and place them in a controlled isolated virtual switch before practice.
A host has only 4 GB RAM and limited SSD storage. Which approach is most responsible?
Disable host memory safeguards and run multiple full guests
Allocate more total guest RAM than the host can provide
Use lightweight browser simulations until hardware and memory allow isolated VMs
A host constrained by 4 GB RAM and limited disk cannot safely run several large guests. Lightweight simulations are more practical until enough resources are available.
What makes a VM snapshot different from a verified backup?
A snapshot copied nowhere else is guaranteed to survive host failure
A snapshot is a point-in-time VM state and may share the host's failure domain
A snapshot intrinsically enforces network isolation
A VM snapshot is a point-in-time state often sharing host storage and failure risk. A separately stored and restore-tested backup provides different protection.
What establishes that a virtual lab is isolated from household and public networks?
Positive and negative connectivity checks confirming route and firewall boundaries
Private IPv4 addresses alone mean no household access exists
A virtual machine labeled isolated must have no external routes
Virtual-network isolation requires inspecting adapters, routing/firewall policies and controlled allowed/denied tests. Private addresses and guest names alone prove little.
Before running a new training tool, which combination best reduces risk?
Use administrator privileges everywhere
Copy the command from a random video
Check its purpose and provenance, confirm authorization and use a disposable isolated environment
Check a training tool's function, provenance and required permissions; use a disposable owned VM and documented rollback before running unfamiliar software.
A Kali Linux VM can ping a training server but HTTP fails. Which step best isolates the cause?
Reinstall the operating system without inspecting service status
Inspect service listener, firewall rules and application HTTP response
Conclude the server is compromised from the HTTP failure
If ping reaches an owned server but HTTP fails, inspect the application listener, port and filtering within authorized lab boundaries. IP reachability is not application health.
A lab guest was saved using a snapshot. What verifies that a later exercise can be repeated?
Restore the snapshot and retest required service, credentials and network conditions
A snapshot description that names the operating system
A saved guest file without verifying startup and connectivity
Snapshot restore should be tested by reproducing the service, account and networking baseline. The mere presence of a snapshot file does not prove repeatability.
When building a Windows/Linux lab, how should privileged lab accounts be managed?
Reuse personal account passwords
Publish them in GitHub for convenience
Separate fictional lab accounts, least-privilege roles and protected credentials
Separate fictional privileged lab identities prevent personal credentials from spreading to practice environments. Least privilege and protected storage apply inside labs too.
What evidence belongs in a home-lab change log?
The final exam score without documenting the system state
Initial state, command or change, observed results, validation and rollback
A Wi-Fi password from a device outside the training scope
Record original state, changes, observed effects, validation and rollback in the lab log. This supports repeatability without collecting unrelated Wi-Fi credentials.
